title: Ponte Vecchio Across the Atlantic: Single-Node Benchmarking of Two Intel GPU Systems
problem: Intel's Ponte Vecchio GPU architecture needs performance characterization on practical HPC systems to help developers understand achievable performance and predict application behavior. The relationship between micro-benchmarking results and real application performance on PVC must be established.
motivation: With Ponte Vecchio-based systems ranking highly on the Top 500 (Aurora #2, Dawn #51), understanding their performance relative to established GPU competitors is critical for HPC system adoption and application development strategies.
method: The researchers used micro-benchmarks—simple tests of basic GPU operations—to understand Ponte Vecchio's capabilities, then validated that these results predicted performance on four test programs whose behavior was already well-understood. They measured performance on single nodes from Aurora and Dawn, two production systems with Ponte Vecchio GPUs, using the same tests on NVIDIA H100 and AMD MI250 GPUs to directly compare results. They also ran actual applications on large Intel GPU systems to demonstrate that these benchmarking insights have practical value.
key_novelty: This is the first measurement of Intel Ponte Vecchio GPU performance on actual production systems (Aurora and Dawn), compared directly against NVIDIA H100 and AMD MI250 GPUs under the same testing conditions.
contributions: Micro-benchmarking data quantifying Ponte Vecchio architectural properties and performance characteristics
Validation that micro-benchmarking results are indicative of mini-app and real application performance on PVC
Performance comparison showing PVC mini-app figure-of-merit ranges from 0.6–1.8X H100 and 0.8–7.5X MI250
Demonstration of real applications running on large-scale Intel GPU systems
limitations: Analysis limited to single-node performance; multi-node scalability, communication overhead, and system-level integration challenges are not addressed.
